Latin word

sub

sub (+ acc.)

preposition: with the ablative for where a thing is, with the accusative for where it goes · Wiktionary

just before (an event); under, beneath

In this lexicon

  • just now

    also used · classical · Traupman 335

  • under

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. ND 2.95: quī sub terrā semper habitāvissent; Cic. Rep. 1.25: cum tōta sē lūna sub orbem sōlis subjēcisset

  • sub dīvō: air

    classical

  • conclāve sub tēctō: attic

    * our formation

  • sub hastā vēndere: auction

    classical

  • lāmina sub fistulā posita: base plate

    * our formation

  • sub + acc.: by

    classical

  • sub pellibus pernoctāre: camping

    * our formation

  • sub dīvō pernoctāre: camping

    * our formation

  • sub noctem: just before nightfall

    classical

  • Adhūc sub jūdice līs est.: the matter is still undecided

    classical
